question: What does an NTR-7 record track, and why is it not a treatment-completion certificate?

- It documents a referral when a nutrition centre hands a child or mother to a health facility (referral initiation) [02_Health_and_Public_Health.txt#page-2-chunk-8].

- Required fields on each NTR-7 include: referral reason, issue date, receiving service point, acceptance status, correction status, and follow-up due date — i.e., the record of coordination and administrative status [02_Health_and_Public_Health.txt#page-2-chunk-9].  
- In short, NTR-7 measures care/referral coordination (administration and follow-up) rather than clinical care itself [02_Health_and_Public_Health.txt#page-2-chunk-10].

Why an NTR-7 is not a treatment-completion certificate
- NTR-7 records coordination and administrative status; it does not record clinical assessment, treatment delivered, or clinical outcomes. question: Why is an ECR-5 action-complete status not proof of environmental compliance?
expected_behavior: Explain that it only shows the corrective action was reported complete; the applicable environmental outcome still requires recorded verification.
llm_response:
Short answer
An ECR-5 “action‑complete” only records that a corrective action was reported complete; it is not proof the environmental outcome was met until a verification record confirms the source/standard is actually compliant [05_Renewable_Energy_and_Power.txt#page-2-chunk-2].

Why (details, kept as separate stages/records)
- What ECR‑5 records: inspected site, the applicable condition, evidence source, corrective owner, due date and a verification result — verification is a distinct field on the form [05_Renewable_Energy_and_Power.txt#page-2-chunk-2].  
- Reported completion ≠ verified outcome: “action‑complete” documents a reported corrective action; it does not by itself demonstrate a water body, airshed or neighbourhood met the outcome standard until verification is recorded [05_Renewable_Energy_and_Power.txt#page-2-chunk-2].  
- Operational difference to check: an installed asset or completed work must still be distinguished from an operating facility, a collected sample, a standard being met, and a verified environmental outcome — each is a different stage and requires verification [05_Renewable_Energy_and_Power.txt#page-2-chunk-1].  
- Where a source is affected (e.g., urban drainage/waste failures), the ECR‑5 evidence must be linked to the source record and the correction path reported so the actual source condition can be confirmed [05_Renewable_Energy_and_Power.txt#page-2-chunk-5].

Supporting parallels (same principle applied elsewhere)
- An SRR‑12 closed entry is not proof a source is restored until the source is verified functional [01_Agriculture_and_Farmers_Welfare.txt#page-2-chunk-13].  
- An administrative closure is not a verified remedy unless the required verification record is present in JGR‑11 [06_Digital_India_and_Public_Services.txt#page-2-chunk-8].  
- Likewise, certificates or declarations (e.g., earthwork completion, infrastructure coverage, ODF status) are not by themselves proof of sustained service, safe water quality or reduced disease without outcome/service verification [10_Rural_Development_and_Livelihoods.txt#page-2-chunk-1; 01_Agriculture_and_Farmers_Welfare.txt#page-3-chunk-0; 01_Agriculture_and_Farmers_Welfare.txt#page-2-chunk-4].

Conclusion
Thus, an ECR‑5 marked action‑complete is only a reported status; environmental compliance requires the separate, recorded verification that demonstrates the relevant standard or service has actually been achieved [05_Renewable_Energy_and_Power.txt#page-2-chunk-2].
